reference.shortHeaderRule: The reference reads its first 4 bytes unconditionally; native decoding explicitly rejects shorter buffers.
reference.timingScope: Only format, PIT periods and callback frequency outputs are compared; the reference 7 ms callback is not used as native scheduler proof.

scope: All 174 DP lumps from official Freedoom 0.13.0 Phase 1/Phase 2 plus 14 format-boundary streams are decoded through native disk reads.
All 78073 payload samples match the pinned reference PIT periods and unchanged callback frequency outputs, including all 256 byte values and the maximum 65535-sample header count.

Short/invalid/truncated headers are rejected, trailing bytes are ignored, empty streams and out-of-range sample indexes are silent. Read-byte accounting proves that only the header and declared payload are read.
Eight constructor fault paths cover header/payload read returns and exceptions plus object/body allocation exceptions; each retains exact heap ownership, and retry succeeds.
limits: The module is not yet included by the playable entry and does not write speaker ports.
No sound prioritization, cache/actor binding, 140 Hz scheduling, focus/mute/pause ownership or audible native/browser claim yet.
The reference callback uses integer 7 ms durations; this gate compares format/period/frequency semantics only.
Short-buffer rejection is an explicit safe extension to the reference code, which otherwise reads four bytes before checking length.
Allocation injection covers application boundaries, not every internal OS allocation.
